reviews.title: Very Disappointing Customer Service – Unfair Baggage Charge
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Ryanair.

When booking my flight, I paid for Priority and 2 Cabin Bags, including my 10 kg cabin bag. However, at the airport, the check-in staff member failed to add my purchased baggage allowance to my boarding pass.

When I arrived at the boarding gate with my bag, I was charged an additional fee, despite having already paid for this baggage service during my booking.

I contacted Ryanair customer service, explained the situation and provided evidence, including my payment receipt. Unfortunately, instead of properly investigating my complaint, I received a generic response referring to Ryanair’s baggage policies.

The issue was not that I failed to follow the baggage rules. The issue was that I had already paid for the service, but an airport staff error resulted in me being charged again.

I find it very disappointing that a company of Ryanair’s size cannot properly investigate a straightforward customer complaint.

I hope Ryanair improves its airport procedures and customer service, and takes responsibility when mistakes are made.

reviews.text:
Complaint Regarding Ryanair’s App and Baggage Booking Process

It seems to be a recurring theme whenever I speak to other people about travelling with Ryanair. You try to log into the app to check in, manage your booking or confirm your baggage allowance, and you are constantly bombarded with prompts to buy this, add that, or pay extra for something else.

What makes the experience particularly frustrating is how confusing the baggage section can be. There are plenty of clear options for purchasing additional bags, but it is far less obvious how to confirm the bags you have already paid for. This creates unnecessary panic and doubt: “Hang on, haven’t I already purchased a bag? Have I done something wrong?” You then find yourself trawling through emails and booking confirmations, questioning your own decisions and worrying that something has gone wrong.

I eventually had to leave the app and access my booking through the website instead. Even there, the process still felt designed in a way that encourages you to panic and purchase additional baggage, because it is not immediately clear whether the baggage you have already paid for has been recognised.

I find this deeply disappointing. I know Ryanair is supposed to be a low-fares airline. However, the entire purchase process feels like it's designed to trip the consumer up at every step. I normally fly with British Airways precisely because I find all of this so awful to use. I will avoid using Ryanair wherever possible.

Yet again, I've been through your website process and spent the entire time trying to avoid being charged for things I don't need. It's deliberately confusing. Charges are put on when you think you've already made a purchase. For example, I've just purchased seats and then discovered I need to pay a transaction charge for card cost.

Everything is hidden, a surprise, even the fact that I have to check in 24 hours before, but not later than 2 hours before, otherwise I'll get a £50 fine for a boarding card. It's all deliberately designed to make money in an illicit way. You should be stopped from doing this by government legislation. None of this is in the interests of the consumer. Isn't it unfortunate that sometimes we just have no choice but to fly with airlines like you?

reviews.text:
The app mostly works (in that the scummy tactics Ryanair uses are fully operational) but toggling between tabs fully freezes my app and requires a restart.
The incredible amount of promotional offers and ads in the app means that it is quite unresponsive, especially on slow connections. The app also seemingly doesn’t have a cookie opt-out, which is mildly worrying!
Can’t wait for the EU to regulate the hell out of Ryanair and end their scummy tactics. Moving away from paper tickets is all well and good, but tickets being available only in-app is a data harvesting tactic.
Of course, you could check in online and then inform gate staff that you have lost your phone, where policy dictates they must then give you a free paper boarding pass!
P.S. there is no functioning in-app opt-out of notifications. If you don’t want Ryanair to advertise to you endlessly, you will have to turn off all notifications in your iPhone’s Settings.

reviews.text:
Disappointing Experience with Ryanair

Very disappointed with my recent experience using the Ryanair app.

While booking our family holiday, I accidentally purchased two additional 20kg checked bags because the app did not make it clear that baggage had already been added to the booking. There was no warning or prompt saying something as simple as, “This passenger already has a checked bag. Do you wish to continue?” A basic confirmation like this could have prevented an expensive mistake.

As an NHS Intensive Care Sister, I was booking after finishing a night shift while trying to look after my children with no sleep. It was an honest error, but one that has cost my family around £250—money we simply cannot afford to lose.

I appreciate that mistakes happen, but good customer service is about recognising genuine errors, especially when they could easily be prevented by better app design. I hope Ryanair will review both my case and the usability of their app so that other families don’t find themselves in the same situation.

Sadly, this experience has left me feeling extremely let down.

reviews.title: Poor Customer Service and Lack of Clear Transit Information
reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience. I travelled to the airport expecting to complete my journey, but I later discovered that I could not board because of transit visa requirements. When I went to the desk to explain my situation and ask for assistance, I felt that the staff were dismissive and unhelpful. Instead of trying to understand my circumstances or discuss possible options, the interaction felt rude and lacked empathy.

I was also frustrated by the lack of clear information regarding self-transfer and transit requirements. Many passengers may not fully understand the difference between a self-transfer itinerary and a protected connection, and I believe this should be explained more clearly during the booking process to help travellers avoid costly mistakes.

As a result, I lost money on flights and accommodation and was left feeling unsupported. I hope customer service training and clearer communication can improve the experience for future passengers.

reviews.title: Good app, but missing a basic Apple Wallet feature
reviews.text:
Overall the Ryanair app works well for managing bookings and boarding passes. However, one major usability gap really stands out.
When travelling as a family or group, there’s no way to “Add All” boarding passes to Apple Wallet in one action. Each ticket has to be added individually, which is tedious and error‑prone when you’re managing multiple passengers (especially with kids).
Other airlines and travel apps already support an “Add All to Wallet” option, so this is clearly technically possible. Adding this would be a small change but a huge improvement to the user experience for families and group travellers.
Please consider prioritising this — it would make the app far more user‑friendly.

The process would be a lot quicker for clients (whose convenience as usual comes in last place with this airline’s priorities) if the A.I. did NOT keep interrupting to urge the client to purchase “travel insurance” (yeah, were talking Ryanair - good luck with that), microwaved cheese sarnies “brought to your seat” (for the price of a wagyu burger) or dodgy transport or accomodation with their “partners” (if the same levels of client satisfaction as Ryanair’s are to be expected, well, no thanks).  All I want is to get boarding cards for me and my Ryanair Staff-proof cabin luggage to get on and off the plane as quickly as possible, but even that seems too much to ask?
